messages:
anna_support: Hey team, customer 'Onlineshop Inc' in Private deployment reporting sudden mTLS handshake failures to our control plane since this morning's NVA firmware push. They see repeated TLS alert + connection resets and our health checks show 503s. Filing here to triage.

lucy_customerops: I have their support ticket attached: says failures started ~07:12 UTC after a firewall update. They've captured a pcap and say only traffic through corp-NVA is affected.

sam_engineer: Thanks. Quick checks: do they route through a TLS-inspecting proxy? Common culprits: SNI rewrite, ALPN strip, or truncation of ClientHello due to TCP MSS/fragmentation.

lucy_customerops: Customer confirms they have an inline NVA doing TLS inspection + app layer policies. They pushed a new signature set at 07:10. PCAP link: https://files.onlineshop/captures/0312.pcap (they uploaded to support bucket).

mike_infra: Can we get a small tcpdump snippet from their egress (first hop) showing the ClientHello handshake? If we can see ClientHello then we can see SNI/ALPN/keyshare. Ask them to run:

```
sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w - 'host controlplane.redwood.private and port 443' | head -c 200000 > clienthello.pcap
```

jess_oncall: Also request an openssl s_client test from their edge to our control plane to confirm what we see without NVA:

```
openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.private:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.private -alpn h2 -tls1_3 -msg
```

lucy_customerops: They ran both. Paste from their openssl (sanitized):

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
write to 0x7f9bfe006c40 [0x7f9bfe019200] (512 bytes => 512 (0x200))
<<< TLS 1.2 ALERT: fatal, decrypt_error
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

sam_engineer: Interesting - alert says decrypt_error and no cert returned. That usually means an intermediary terminated or altered the handshake before upstream responded. In TLS-inspect setups we often see either:
- proxy re-signing with its own cert but failing client auth (mTLS)
- proxy truncating ClientHello (small MSS or NVA bug)
- SNI removed/changed so upstream doesn't select client-certificate policy

mike_infra: From the pcap they shared (I fetched), the ClientHello appears to be fragmented: second TCP segment carrying extensions is not forwarded intact; we see ClientHello length 0x... then a TCP RST from proxy. Snippet: `ClientHello (partial), extensions missing: server_name, supported_versions, key_share`. That aligns with the new NVA signature set dropping large TLS records.

lucy_customerops: Customer notes the ClientHello size is ~1200 bytes (lots of ALPN + kcaches). They say previously NVA allowed this.

sam_engineer: That points to either MSS/mss-clamping or the NVA truncating on policy. Ask them to temporarily disable TLS inspection for controlplane.redwood.private and test. If that fixes it we can mark it as NVA-as-inspector issue. Also request that they allowlist our control plane IPs and ensure ALPN+SNI passthrough.

lucy_customerops: They tried disabling inspection for that FQDN — on first try they got a successful handshake and we saw our normal cert chain and the mTLS client cert being forwarded. So that's a repro path forward.

jess_oncall: Good. Next steps: 1) recommend a permanent allowlist/ bypass rule for controlplane.redwood.private for TLS inspection 2) if they must inspect, ask vendor to upgrade NVA or enable "large TLS record passthrough"/MSS clamping fix 3) provide ops steps to verify (pcap on both sides).

mike_infra: Also callout: if their NVA re-signs traffic, mutual TLS will always break because our control plane expects client certs presented to upstream. A re-signing proxy will terminate the client cert before it reaches us. So bypass is required unless they do passthrough mode.

lucy_customerops: Customer asked if we can accept a fallback connection (non-mTLS) temporarily. Jess, is that allowed?

jess_oncall: We cannot accept non-mTLS control-plane connections for Private deployments per policy. Security constraints require mTLS. We can provide a temporary support window if they create a direct NAT path that bypasses the NVA.

sam_engineer: For their engineers — concrete repro checklist to send:
- capture pcap at egress right at NVA ingress and at the NAT egress to cloud
- run `openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.private:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.private -alpn h2 -tls1_3 -msg` from their edge with/without inspection
- run `curl -v --http2 --tlsv1.3 https://controlplane.redwood.private/health` from same host and paste verbose output
- include NVA config (policy rule for that FQDN) and MSS/MTU settings

mike_infra: I also recommended they check for ALPN stripping. If ALPN removed, our control plane may not advertise h2 and handshake flows differ.

lucy_customerops: They provided NVA rule dump (redacted) — policy shows FQDN match but action=INSPECT with default re-signing cert. Customer is trying to change to action=BYPASS now and will retest in 10m.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance notice — NVA vendor has a hotfix for TLS truncation (ticket #NV-1123). ETA for patch depends on customer approval.

anna_support: Thanks all. Customer confirmed bypass -> immediate success. They've opened an internal change to bypass control plane FQDN permanently. I'll document the workaround and follow up with NVA vendor patch plan. Marking as high priority until permanent fix is in.

sam_engineer: Filed internal follow-up: ENG-RUNTIME to add a KB entry for "Private control plane: known TLS-inspection incompatibilities" and recommended bypass patterns (SNI-based allowance, IP allowlist, MTU clamp settings).

jess_oncall: If the customer can't bypass, we can coordinate a support window to test alternative NAT path. I'll own scheduling.

lucy_customerops: Customer will confirm when their change is live. I'll update ticket. :thumbsup:

anna_support: Closing this thread for now until customer updates. Thanks everyone.
